- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for negative sentiment.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00 followed by high forecast), especially in early 30d horizon — cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast > 1.5x recent 7-day high, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment is strong.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is > 2x recent 7-day high, model is likely overconfident — apply downward correction based on sentiment decay (e.g., if sentiment drops after spike, reduce forecast by 30–50%).
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction, not just price history.
